31 October 2026 · Working concept · Name provisional

## Current decision
Build a real Photo Frame Commons experiment around [wesbos/photo-frame-dashboard](https://github.com/wesbos/photo-frame-dashboard). The purpose is discoverable experience and shared sensemaking in an agent-mediated web. It must make sense with or without the Adobe/PDF narrative.

For these two days, the active repositories are:

- **[baselhack26-knowledge-lab](https://github.com/blackmath88/baselhack26-knowledge-lab):** the parallel graph/retrieval learning experiment. Build and explore a graph for fun; investigate what it reveals and what its extraction loses.

Postack Underflow and br-ai-nstorm supply research and reusable mechanisms. They are not additional weekend delivery destinations. This supersedes the earlier suggestion to implement the pilot inside Postack at /commons/. Wes's repository remains an external source, not a repository we modify.

## Our two repos for these two days
| Repository | Focus |
| --- | --- |
| **This repository** | The photo-frame pilot, discovery/community experience and optional Adobe story |
| **[Knowledge Lab](https://github.com/blackmath88/baselhack26-knowledge-lab)** | Build and explore a graph for fun; investigate extraction, relationships and retrieval with LightRAG |

The graph is part of the exploration. Its connections must lead back to evidence and disclose how they were proposed. A simpler local index keeps the pilot usable independently of the lab service.

[Postack Underflow](https://github.com/blackmath88/postack-underflow) and [br-ai-nstorm](https://github.com/blackmath88/br-ai-nstorm) are prior work and reuse sources, not extra weekend delivery repos. **Build the new pilot here**, superseding the earlier suggestion to put it in Postack. Wes's repository stays the external source.

# Hackathon plan — Photo Frame Commons
31 October–1 November 2026 · Europe/Zurich (UTC+01:00)

## Finish line
One person can ask a real photo-frame question, inspect relevant experiences and their limits, follow original sources, explore attributable connections, and draft a small follow-up without publishing it.

Alongside that, explore a passage-grounded graph in Knowledge Lab. The user experience must remain usable from a local snapshot if the lab is unavailable. Adobe/PDF is an optional presentation, not a prerequisite.

## Current state
Concept and repo scope are established. Implementation, corpus import and live graph results are not marked complete. Knowledge Lab has prior work on continuation branches; its runtime must be checked rather than inferred from its older main README.

NOW: select the bounded corpus for “My Mac cannot see my frame,” check Knowledge Lab's active state, and agree the export boundary.

records.excerpt:
## What we want to learn
Compare ordinary repository navigation with our pilot on a small set of real questions:
- Can someone find an applicable account?
- Can they explain why a similar account does not apply?
- Can they distinguish an observed result, a source claim and our interpretation?
- Can they reach the original conversation and identify what remains unknown?
- Can they draft a useful follow-up without losing their own voice or exposing unrelated private context?

For the graph: does it reveal a useful relationship, or merely create an appealing but misleading picture? Compare with the simpler index; record failures.

A small test may demonstrate a discovery mechanism. Community value requires people using it over time. Do not call the theory proven because a graph renders or a demo succeeds.
